transcript.title: Opening
transcript.text: Good morning Rushil Bhatia. Here is your daily news for Tuesday, November 24. In today's briefing: top headlines, bhopal and madhya pradesh, business and markets, money, tax and personal finance, science and technology, development and policy, across india, around the world. Let's begin.

transcript.title: Top headlines
transcript.text: First, the stories leading the news this morning. NCP leader's drunk son runs over moped killing 2, drives home and goes to sleep. In a tragic incident in Kolhapur, a man named Padmasinh Ranjitsinh Patil, while intoxicated, struck two cousins on a moped, resulting in their fatal injuries. Following the collision, he fled the scene, oblivious to the severity of the accident. Later that evening, police arrested him as they compiled evidence. The victims' families are now pursuing justice and compensation for their devastating loss. 'It was done on purpose': Sonia, Rahul revisit Rajiv's security withdrawal. Sonia Gandhi has alleged that former Prime Minister Rajiv Gandhi's security was deliberately withdrawn to facilitate his assassination. In a conversation with Rahul and Priyanka Gandhi about her book 'Belonging: A Journey of Love', she recalled raising concerns over his safety, including during a Bihar tour. Rahul also alleged that there was an intention behind the decision, saying his mother had left out some details from the book. rupees 5 khaini packet proves costly for UP man in Bahrain. Saurabh Rai, a 35-year-old man from Azamgarh, was detained in Bahrain after customs found khaini and lime. He spent 18 days in custody and faced severe questioning regarding his possession. His family arranged a lawyer and paid a fine of nearly rupees 18 lakh for his release. After returning home, he is currently receiving treatment for typhoid and malaria. Priyansh Arya rewrites history, breaks KL Rahul's record for highest T20 score. Priyansh Arya, the captain of Delhi, delivered an extraordinary performance in the Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy by scoring 181 runs. His remarkable innings featured an incredible 19 sixes, breaking KL Rahul's previous record for a T20 innings. Delhi finished strong, amassing a total of 275 runs for five wickets, moving Arya to second place in the highest individual scores of men's T20 cricket, marking a significant moment in T20 history. Google responds to 'huge layoffs' in India report. Google has responded to rumors of significant layoffs in its India operations that emerged recently. The company clarified that only approximately 30 roles were eliminated as part of a small reorganization. Reports suggested that team members were receiving termination notices unrelated to performance concerns. However, these claims about potential January layoffs and severance packages remain unverified. Chinese scientist's 40-year effort helps Yangtze porpoise population rise 40 percent. For more than four decades, Dr. Wang Ding has been at the forefront of research on freshwater cetaceans, focusing on the Yangtze finless porpoise. After the tragic extinction of the Yangtze River dolphin, his committed conservation efforts have led to a notable rise in porpoise numbers, with an increase from 1,012 to 1,426 between 2017 and 2025 as estimated by the IUCN. 2nd Test: Mitchell hopes Hagley pitch favours bowlers, says NZ were happy with draw. Daryl Mitchell is gearing up for a tougher battle in the second Test against India at Hagley Oval. He observed that the pitch might provide more bounce and bowler-friendly conditions. Following a stalemate in the first Test, he highlighted that both sides can take away valuable insights. With ample recovery time for the New Zealand bowlers, Mitchell is confident that the team is well-acquainted with the conditions at Hagley Oval. At least four affairs? New report adds to Jensen Huang scandal after Nvidia comeback. Reinstated Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang reportedly disclosed additional extramarital affairs during a lengthy meeting with the company's board on Sunday. Rising toll: Why Delhi continues to struggle with road safety. Fatal road accidents in Delhi saw a significant increase by 7.7 percent compared to the same period last year. The total number of accidents rose by 13 percent from the previous year, highlighting alarming trends. Key factors contributing to these accidents include speeding and inadequate road infrastructure, according to officials. Experts emphasized the need for institutional accountability and greater investment in road safety measures. Flydubai's Tel Aviv flights to resume within weeks, 2 months after hijack bid. Flydubai has received approval from Israeli transportation minister Miri Regev to resume its flights to Tel Aviv. The approval came after a meeting where security arrangements were discussed to ensure safe operations. The airline previously suspended services after an incident involving an attempted hijacking by an Omani co-pilot. Services are expected to restart pending clearance from Israel's security establishment in the coming weeks. Australian 16m bamboo hedge row ends with cutback order and split fence costs. A legal battle arose between Leonard Clyde Lloyd and Susan Boyd Valstar over a bamboo hedge in Australia. The Land and Environment Court ordered the removal of bamboo growing on the boundary. Lloyd's complaints included property damage and reduced sunlight due to the bamboo's height. The court ruled that vegetation contributed minimally to fence damage and ordered equal cost sharing for its replacement.

Investors seeking income from equities may note that CyberTech Systems, Majestic Auto, Jagran Prakashan, IL and FS Investment Managers, and Premco Global recorded yields as high as 19.6 percent , exceeding the roughly 8 percent –8.6 percent offered by fixed deposits. Foodlink F and B Holdings' rupees 361 crore IPO to open for subscription on Nov 26. Foodlink F and B Holdings (India) Ltd, a luxury food services company, is looking to raise rupees 361 crore through its maiden public offering, which will open for subscription on November 26, with a price band of rupees 181-191 per share. The Initial Public Offering (IPO) will close on November 30, while bidding for anchor investors will take place on November 25, according to the public announcement on Monday. The public issue comprises a fresh issue of equity shares aggregating up to rupees 192 crore and an Offer For Sale (OFS) of up to 88,35,382 equity shares worth rupees 168.76 crore by existing shareholders. At the upper end of the price band, the total issue size works out to rupees 360.76 crore. Bottled water's clean image faces a murky test. Analyst Chandan Taparia recommended Persistent Systems and Ather Energy shares to buy tomorrow. NSEL releases rupees 1,950 cr in one-time settlement, ends 14-yr payment default. The National Spot Exchange Ltd (NSEL) on Monday said it has released a one-time settlement (OTS) payout of rupees 1,950 crore to eligible claimants, bringing closure to the rupees 5,600 crore payment default crisis after nearly 14 years of legal battle. The Mumbai bench of the National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT) had approved the settlement scheme. The full amount was deposited in a settlement account, with payouts to eligible specified creditors scheduled for November 23, 2026. The money was paid to 63 Moons Technologies, which acted as assignee of the specified creditors. Huang's return sends S Korea's AI stocks soaring. US President Donald Trump shared an AI-generated image of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang recreating his iconic fist-raising pose after the 2024 assassination attempt, with a red undergarment in his hand and an Nvidia flag in the background.

Can the India–US tax treaty or an NRE account make Indian rental income tax-free?. The India-US tax treaty provides relief through eligible foreign tax credits in the US, while interest earned on the NRE balance may be tax-exempt. BSE, Motherson, Zetwerk, Max Healthcare and JSW Dulux also featured among the top stocks bought across market-cap segments. RBI proposes new rules to protect bank accounts from fraud; here's how Stop Switch and trusted person approval work. RBI has proposed a Stop Switch to block outgoing bank payments, customer-set digital transaction limits and a trusted person mechanism for approving high-value transfers. The draft rules also seek to strengthen banks' accountability for digital payment fraud. CRIF High Mark is now CRIF Credit Information Services: What borrowers should know. CRIF provides credit information and analytics to banks, non-banking financial companies (NBFCs), housing finance companies and microfinance institutions, among other lenders. DSP Mutual Fund set to boost gold and silver exposure: Inside its price-based buying strategy. Rather than increasing exposure during market rallies, DSP plans to accumulate the metals in phases as international prices decline. The fund house said the pace of purchases could be adjusted depending on market conditions.

transcript.text: Next, science and technology. AI adoption to sustain demand for Indian IT services firms; labour-based models face pressure: Report. India's IT services companies could continue to benefit from the growing adoption of artificial intelligence as businesses require support for integrating AI solutions, managing data and deploying them at scale, even as automation puts pressure on traditional labour-based delivery models, according to a Systematix report. Google alternative Kagi launches an email service. Kagi, which already offers a paid alternative to Google Search and its own Orion browser as a rival to Chrome, is taking on another Google service: Gmail. Today, Kagi announced a public beta of Kagi Mail, a new email service that has "no surveillance, no ads, open standards, and no lock-in." With Kagi Mail, you Figma employee sues, alleging company forced her to confront harassers. Figma and its CEO are being sued by a current employee for alleged sexual harassment and discrimination. New gum disease treatment kills bad bacteria while sparing the good. Researchers in Japan have developed an innovative gum disease treatment that uses egg yolk antibodies and near-infrared light to destroy harmful bacteria without harming beneficial microbes. Unlike conventional treatments, the approach preserves the mouth's natural bacterial balance and protects healthy gum cells. In mice, it significantly reduced the bone loss associated with periodontitis, a major cause of tooth loss. Secret recording, AI errors and privacy risks: Why Dutch watchdog is against camera glasses. The Dutch Data Protection Authority has urged consumers not to buy AI-powered camera glasses, warning that they pose serious privacy and safety risks. The regulator also flagged cases of AI errors and said recording people in public using these devices is almost always prohibited. The hacker behind early GTA VI leaks has been sentenced , and released. Arion Kurtaj, who pleaded guilty last week to hacking Grand Theft Auto VI developer Rockstar Games and other companies, including Uber and Revolut, was sentenced to seven years in prison but released on license, the BBC reports. After hacking Rockstar, Kurtaj leaked 90 videos of GTA VI in 2022, years before the game's public release Anthropic launches Claude Ship, letting AI agents review, fix, and approve code changes. As AI-generated code piles up, Anthropic's new developer tools aim to eliminate another bottleneck by letting agents handle routine approvals. This tiny spider named after Stephen Colbert has a genome 50 percent larger than a human's. A tiny California trapdoor spider named after Stephen Colbert has a genome roughly 50 percent larger than a human's, despite being only about the size of a quarter. Scientists discovered that its enormous genome contains 4.6 billion DNA base pairs and 52 chromosomes, revealing surprising clues about spider evolution. Engineer turns batteries from 500 discarded vapes into a power pack that ran his home for eight hours. Electronics engineer Chris Doel recovered 500 lithium batteries from discarded vapes and built a 2.5kWh battery pack. The system powered his home appliances, including a microwave and kettle, for eight hours without using electricity from the grid. The Verge's 2026 holiday gift guide. Gift-giving isn't just about grabbing something solid under a determined spending limit. It's an expression of love, a way to show someone how well you really know them. That doesn't mean you have to do it all on your own, though. Sometimes you just need a push in the right direction to get things rolling. Astronomers have discovered the oldest known compact pair of quasars, powered by two enormous black holes that existed just 900 million years after the Big Bang. Weighing an astonishing 1.5 billion and 400 million times the mass of the Sun, these cosmic giants somehow grew to incredible sizes far earlier than current theories can explain. The company may split the launches across February, March and April. Ladybird, the first new browser engine in years, is now available to test. Ladybird, an independent web browser with a built-from-scratch engine, is finally available for testing. On Monday, Ladybird developer Andreas Kling announced that the browser is launching in alpha on macOS and Linux following more than four years of development. The release makes Ladybird the first browser in years to arrive with an entirely new engine. Elon Musk and others rejoice as Jensen Huang is reinstated at Nvidia amid scandal. "The mistake has been corrected," Elon Musk chimed in. Archaeologists reveal a powerful Iron Age king may have been a woman. Archaeologists have uncovered evidence that Verica, the Iron Age ruler whose exile helped trigger Rome's invasion of Britain in AD 43, was actually a woman. The discovery challenges centuries of historical assumptions and suggests that a largely forgotten female leader may have changed the course of British history. Vivo S70, S70 flagship edition to launch in December: Check expected features and camera details. Vivo has confirmed that the S70 series, comprising the Vivo S70 and S70 flagship edition, will launch in China in December 2026, with pre-orders now open. Trump engineered a risky comeback for Jensen Huang. After Nvidia's board accepted Jensen Huang's resignation as CEO, following reports that Huang had an affair with an alleged Chinese spy, President Donald Trump, too, appeared to submit to the new reality. Appearing on Stephen A. Smith's radio show shortly after the news came out, Trump said that Huang would "end up on his feet." Megaspeed, the company at the center of the Jensen Huang scandal, appears headed for a US blacklist. Megaspeed, which was previously led by Alice Huang, would be barred from doing business with U.S. companies unless those companies attained a special license from the federal government. Mice slept 70 percent less after scientists switched off these brain cells. Scientists have discovered brain cells that actively generate the irresistible urge to sleep, and shutting them down allowed mice to sleep 70 percent less than normal. Remarkably, many of the animals avoided the severe behavioral consequences of sleep deprivation, raising intriguing possibilities for future sleep research. Motorola Edge 70 Neo India launch on November 24: Check expected price, 7,000mAh battery, camera and other features. Motorola Edge 70 Neo will launch in India on 24 November with a 7,000mAh battery, 144Hz AMOLED display and Snapdragon 7s Gen 3 processor. Here is everything to know about its camera, charging, features, expected price and availability. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is back. What happens next?. After the leather-jacketed CEO, president, and co-founder of Nvidia, Jensen Huang, acknowledged an affair with Megaspeed exec Alice Huang, his company initially announced an investigation. However, after The New York Times reported there was evidence of another affair, this time with an Nvidia executive who reported directly to him, a board meeting that night ended Nvidia employees greet Jensen Huang like a hero as he returns to company's HQ. "I'm going to be a better CEO the second time around," Huang told employees.

Rahul also alleged that there was an intention behind the decision, saying his mother had left out some details from the book. Observing children should not be treated as toys in the custody battle between parents, Supreme Court Monday said such cases should not be decided only on a legalistic basis but children's choice should be given due weightage while deciding the case.
